Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Enedis nor with MyElectricalData.

> **Status**: this integration has never been tested with a real Linky meter. It is written from the
> public API description of MyElectricalData (its Swagger, version 1.5.15) and from the Enedis data
> formats. Your feedback is welcome.

[MyElectricalData](https://www.myelectricaldata.fr/) is a free community gateway to the Enedis data of
your Linky meter. This integration reads, for each meter (PDL) you enter:

- the **energy of each day** (kWh), shown on the device (a dated value per day): it never feeds the
  costs of Gladys;
- on request, the **30-minute consumption** (load curve): the only data that feeds the energy monitoring
  costs and the energy contracts;
- on request, the **daily peak power** (VA) and the **daily production** (solar panels);
- the **off-peak hours** of the meter (its Enedis contract), which feed the `linky-offpeak` tariff
  calendar of the "Linky peak / off-peak (hours of the meter)" contract template.

Read-only: nothing is ever changed on your account nor on your meter.

## Setup

1. On [myelectricaldata.fr](https://www.myelectricaldata.fr/), give your consent to Enedis for your
   meter and copy the **token** the site gives you.
2. In Gladys, install the integration and fill in:
   - **MyElectricalData token**: kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to
     MyElectricalData;
   - **Meter number(s) (PDL)**: the 14 digits of your PDL (bill or Linky screen), leading zeros kept;
     several separated by commas (5 at most). The off-peak calendar follows the **first** one;
   - the options: **30-minute load curve** (the load curve collection must be enabled for your meter in
     your Enedis customer area), **daily peak power** (on by default), **daily production**.
3. Press **Test the access**: for each meter, the gateway says whether the access is valid, until when
   the consent runs and how many calls it counted.
4. In **Discovery**, create the "Linky meter …1234" device (only the last 4 digits of the PDL are shown).
   Its data is read a minute later: 31 days of energy per day, of peak power and of production, 7 days of
   load curve.

## The energy contract with the real off-peak hours

Create an energy contract on the Linky meter from the **"Linky peak / off-peak (hours of the meter)"**
template and enter your peak and off-peak prices per kWh (taxes included) and your monthly subscription.

**This template needs the "30-minute load curve" option.** Only the half hours feed the costs: Gladys
would price a daily total as one interval stamped at midnight, at the price of the first half hour of
the day (all off-peak with 22:00-06:00), so the energy of each day is published for display only.
Without the load curve, **no cost is computed** at all, and the status says so. With it, every half hour
is priced at its own price.

Ticking or unticking the option never removes a feature: the device offered in Discovery keeps every
feature already created (and its history). Ticking it adds the 30-minute feature: update the device in
Discovery (the status reminds you); the energy of the days goes on meanwhile, no day is lost. The load
curve starts 7 days back (the Enedis limit of one request).

The off-peak half hours are not typed by you: they come from the contract data of your meter, read every
day. Under the Enedis changes of 2025-2027 (part of the off-peak hours moved to the afternoon), the new
hours of your meter are taken up within a day, with nothing to change in Gladys.

- The calendar is published from today to 6 days ahead, one value per half hour of the local time of
  France (46 or 50 on the days of the changes of time).
- A half hour is off-peak when the off-peak hours cover its middle minute (xx:15 or xx:45). A meter
  switching at 22:38 makes 22:30-23:00 off-peak; one switching at 22:15 makes 22:00-22:30 off-peak and
  06:00-06:30 peak. The exact hours are shown on the device (`offpeak_hours` parameter).
- The days between two reads that give the same hours are filled with them (31 days at most). When the
  hours change, only the days from the read on get the new ones.
- A half hour without calendar value (the integration stopped for more than 6 days, a contract starting
  before the installation) is priced at the **peak** price: Gladys never guesses an off-peak hour.
- If the meter has no off-peak hours in its Enedis contract, or if they cannot be read, the calendar is
  not fed and the status says so.
- If another integration already declares the `linky-offpeak` calendar, this one does not feed it.

## How often, and the quotas

The gateway is a free service: the integration asks for little.

- One read a day, from 09:00 (local time of France; a minute between 09:00 and 11:00 proper to your
  installation), asking only for the days not yet published. Enedis gives the data of a day the next
  morning.
- While yesterday is missing: again 3 hours later, at most 3 ordinary reads a day; then the next
  morning. The reads after a pause, a new device or a changed configuration come on top, but the ceiling
  below always holds.
- A new device, or a new token or meter in the configuration: read a minute later.
- At most 12 requests per meter and per day, counted before each request and kept in `/data` (a restart
  does not reset the count).
- A "slow down" answer (429) pauses every request, for the time asked (or 1 hour, then 2, 4, up to
  6 hours); a request already in the queue is held too. A gateway error (5xx) on one route of one meter
  (the load curve not collected, say) makes that route wait: it is tried again at the next ordinary read,
  never sooner than 15 minutes (doubled up to 6 hours, back to 15 minutes after a success), and the
  status gives the real time of that read. The other routes and meters go on, and each read starts with
  another meter. When nothing answered and several routes (or a contract) failed, every request
  pauses (15 minutes, doubled up to 6 hours). A pause is kept across a restart; one ending in the
  night waits for the morning read.
- A request waiting in the queue when a pause starts is not sent.
- The test button asks once per meter, at most once a minute.

## What is published, and when

- **Energy of the day**: each day once, a dated value (the local midnight) shown on the device, never
  priced (no index: nothing can go down). A day corrected later by Enedis is not published again. After a
  stop, up to 92 days are caught up. A day missing from an answer stops
  the publication there: it and the days after it are asked again at the next read (Enedis is sometimes
  late); a day still missing 5 days later is given up.
- **30-minute consumption**: the only consumption sent to the costs (dated consumption of Gladys); whole
  days only (every half hour of the day known once); an hourly curve is
  split in two halves, a 10 or 15-minute curve summed. At most the last 7 days (the Enedis limit of one
  request): a gap longer than that is not filled.
- **Peak power and production**: dated states (the time of the peak; the local midnight for the
  production), by batches of 100, at most 250 a minute. After a long stop, only the last 31 days are
  caught up. A peak of 0 is left out.
- A value that is not a number, a day given twice with two values, an answer about another meter or in
  another unit: left out, never published as 0.
- Gladys should run in the Europe/Paris time zone: the days of Enedis are days of France.

## Refusals and errors

- **Refused**: when the contract of **every** meter is answered 401 or 403 in the same read, the token is
  taken as refused: no request is sent any more, until you press **Test the access** with success or
  change the token or the meter numbers, even while the integration is stopped (a mistyped PDL is
  refused too). A 401/403 on a data route, or on one meter only, is not a refusal (the status
  names the meter and the route).
- The token and the PDL number are never written in the logs, the status nor `/data`. `/data` keeps a
  keyed hash of each meter, the last day published per kind of data, the off-peak hours read, the count
  of requests of the day, the pause and 8 bits of a salted hash of a refused token.
- The device ids come from a key made once and kept in the Gladys configuration (not in the form).
- The devices not read from Gladys at a start: tried again 30 seconds later (doubled up to
  5 minutes); the status says so and nothing is published meanwhile.
- `/data` that cannot be read, or whose write fails: the reads wait an hour after a start (the count of
  the day cannot be trusted) and the status says so. A slow write that lands is fine.

## Limits

- Never tested with a real meter; the stamp of the load curve (end of each interval, as Enedis documents
  it) is checked against each answer but not against real data.
- The days before the installation are priced at the peak price by the template.
- The template needs the load curve: a meter without load curve collection gets no cost computed.
- Several meters: the calendar follows the first one only.

## Data

Data from Enedis, relayed by MyElectricalData under your consent. MyElectricalData is a community
project not affiliated with Enedis.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt MyElectricalData (Linky) in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MyElectricalData account | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Enedis nor with MyElectricalData. MyElectricalData is a free community gateway to the Enedis data of your Linky meter: give your Enedis consent on myelectricaldata.fr, then copy the token it gives you. The integration reads once a day the days not yet published (energy of each day, shown only; on request the 30-minute load curve, the only data that feeds the energy costs; the daily peak power and the production) and the off-peak hours of your meter. Read-only. For an energy contract, tick the load curve, then create it from the "Linky peak / off-peak (hours of the meter)" template: its off-peak slots follow the real hours of your meter. |
| MyElectricalData token | `secret` | Ja | The token myelectricaldata.fr gives once the Enedis consent is done. Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, sent only to MyElectricalData (www.myelectricaldata.fr). |
| Meter number(s) (PDL) | `string` | Ja | The 14 digits of your PDL (on your bill, or on the Linky screen), leading zeros kept; several separated by commas (5 at most). The off-peak calendar follows the first one. Sent only to MyElectricalData; Gladys shows its last 4 digits only. |
| 30-minute load curve | `boolean` | Nein | Reads the consumption of every half hour (from 7 days back): the only data that feeds the energy costs of Gladys, REQUIRED for any energy contract. Needs the load curve collection enabled for your meter (Enedis customer area). Adds a feature: update the device in Discovery (nothing is removed). |
| Daily peak power | `boolean` | Nein | Reads the highest power (VA) reached each day. One more request a day. |
| Daily production | `boolean` | Nein | Only for a meter that also counts a production (solar panels): reads the energy produced each day. One more request a day. |

## So installierst du MyElectricalData (Linky) in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: MyElectricalData (Linky) erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-myelectricaldata:0.1.1`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-myelectricaldata](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-myelectricaldata).

MyElectricalData (Linky) benötigt Gladys `>=5.3.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

MyElectricalData (Linky) ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
